title: Open Syllable
territory: A speech vessel with a subtle M in its filled silhouette and open negative space.
oneSentenceMeaning: An open speech vessel gives your words a clear shape, with Mluva's initial quietly built into its mouth.
appIdentity: Mluva means speech or manner of speaking in Czech. It is an open-source dictation and rewriting app for Omarchy, designed to make speaking feel like an ordinary, pleasant part of working at a computer. A shortcut opens a brief space for speech; the result becomes editable text, with the original recognition retained alongside subsequent work. Local and cloud providers remain explicit choices. Exact source, Markdown, and reviewable rewrites give the calm surface a dependable foundation. This concept expresses the promise, 'Most delightful dictation for Omarchy', through an immediately recognizable place for speech. Its delight comes from the ease of forming and keeping a thought, rather than spectacle or a claim of perfect automation. The identity should sit comfortably beside terminal typography and changing desktop themes, then close a film with 'A little more delight every day'. This is a selection study; the existing production identity remains authoritative until Daniel chooses a direction.
markIdentity: Open Syllable is a solid speech vessel whose upper edge opens into a deliberate central valley. The two shoulders and the valley suggest an M without placing a letter inside an icon. A short tail at the lower left supplies the primary reading: someone has spoken. The broad, connected lower body gives the thought somewhere to settle, while the open notch suggests that more can be said and the resulting text can still be shaped. This is an interpretation of speech and editability, not an encoding of a provider, privacy guarantee, or technical pipeline. The mark borrows the existing identity's generous filled curves, single-color confidence, and quiet movement, but adds a semantic anchor that survives without a written explanation. At a glance it should register as speech; on a second look the M rewards attention. There is one body, one opening, and one speaking tail. Its character is composed, receptive, and lightly human, with no facial expression.
logoDescription:
Create one compact, filled speech vessel with an open central notch in its upper edge. Begin with a broad body, approximately 1.25 times wider than the body is tall. The sides are close to vertical through their middle sections, then turn through generous, continuous corners into a low, gently bowed base. This gives the silhouette a settled, useful presence. Avoid a perfect oval and avoid the domed twin lobes of a heart. The outer body should feel softly formed but deliberately drawn, with short, almost level shoulders on either side of the opening.

The opening is the distinguishing feature. From the inner end of each shoulder, an oblique edge descends towards a shallowly rounded central vertex. Together those edges cut a generous V into the upper half of the solid body. They expose the real transparent background rather than a white inset. The short upper shoulders, descending inner edges, and substantial outer flanks imply a capital M. Keep that inference subordinate to the speech vessel. Do not add an M glyph, another internal cutout, a mouth line, punctuation, or an inset symbol. Below the notch, leave a substantial connected mass; the mark must never look like a thin ribbon or an outlined chat bubble.

A single short tail grows directly from the lower-left quarter of the body and points down and slightly left. It is a broad triangular extension with a softly blunted tip, joined tangentially along its outer edge. Its inner return is concise enough to make the speech-bubble reading unmistakable. The tail occupies roughly one eighth of the total height and does not become a second lobe, a dangling stroke, or a long decorative flourish. The base beyond the tail remains broad and nearly level, preventing a heart reading.

Use a single opaque, very dark ink fill on real transparent alpha. The same geometry must support a light monochrome version later. Center its perceived mass, allowing for the tail, rather than merely centering its bounds. Retain calm continuous curvature, clear negative space, and enough interior substance for the 24-pixel launcher or panel view. The result should feel like a contemporary piece of purposeful software: speech offered a clear, comfortable shape. Generate only the isolated symbol, without a tile, lettering, border, surrounding composition, texture, lighting, gradient, or shadow.
wordmarkDescription:
Draw the exact word 'Mluva', with a capital M followed by lowercase l, u, v, and a. Use JetBrains Mono Medium as the structural starting point: its clear verticals, generous lowercase height, recognizable double-storey a, and matter-of-fact software character should remain visible. Convert the concept to custom filled lettering through controlled optical work. The word should read fluently at once and feel related to the symbol through proportions and curvature, rather than carrying a small speech bubble inside a letter.

Make the M slightly broader than its default cell. Keep the outer stems upright and give the central valley a small amount of additional depth, echoing the symbol's open upper notch without making an ornamental initial. The M should remain unmistakably typographic. Lightly soften only the tightest exterior corners, at a scale barely noticed in the finished word. Maintain the structural contrast between firm vertical sides and the open central gesture. Do not join the M to the next letter.

Narrow the l's allotted width while retaining its recognizable top flag and curved lower foot. This follows the existing identity's useful optical correction and avoids an empty monospaced interval in the middle of the name. Give the u a generous, continuous bottom turn, and keep its right stem and terminal clear. The v should retain its straight diagonal construction, with a minimally blunted bottom point for equal apparent weight. Preserve the a's enclosed lower counter and open upper aperture; enlarge those spaces slightly if needed for reduction.

Resolve spacing by the visible white intervals, not the original font cells. Keep a distinct breath between M and l, then let l, u, v, and a form an even, gently flowing rhythm. The l must not read as part of a ligature, and the u-v pair must not become a w. Use one baseline, one weight, opaque dark ink, and actual transparent alpha. Supply only this exact wordmark. No symbol, tagline, punctuation, alternate spelling, specimen label, background, lighting, or mockup belongs in its generated image.

selfCritique.subject: logo
selfCritique.initialApproach: A plump speech bubble with two fully rounded upper lobes, a deep central cleft, and a soft lower-left tail.
selfCritique.strengths: A clear speech association, a compact connected silhouette, and a gentle relationship to the current abstract mark.
selfCritique.critique: The twin domes and deep cleft made the first construction vulnerable to a heart reading. The small rounded tail could disappear into the body at 24 pixels, leaving an emotive heart or generic blob. Too much organic softness also weakened the deliberate M structure.
selfCritique.revisedDecision: Flatten the upper shoulders slightly, retain short vertical sections in the flanks, use a wide V with a softly rounded vertex, and make the tail a short, broad directional extension. Keep the lower body broad and almost level. These changes anchor speech first and the M second.

selfCritique.subject: wordmark
selfCritique.initialApproach: A softened JetBrains Mono derivative with the full speech notch repeated in the M and a shortened l with almost no top flag.
selfCritique.strengths: The broad M and curved u could carry the same calm voice as the symbol, while an optically narrow l improved the word's rhythm.
selfCritique.critique: Repeating the icon's full notch made the M conspicuous and pushed the rest of the name into a supporting role. Removing the l flag made the exact spelling less secure, especially near the M. Generalized corner rounding diluted JetBrains Mono's useful software character.
selfCritique.revisedDecision: Reduce the M intervention to slight breadth and valley-depth adjustments, restore a clear l flag and foot, keep the v angular, and soften only the tightest corners. Preserve the double-storey a and tune spacing through ordinary optical judgment.

revision.logo: Changed the initial domed, heart-prone upper silhouette into a broad speech body with short level shoulders, straighter flanks, a wide central V, a settled base, and a more explicit short tail.
revision.wordmark: Reduced symbolic intervention in the M, restored the l's identity, retained angular construction in the v, and confined softening to minor optical correction.
revision.appliedTo: Both long descriptions and both generation prompts describe the revised concepts.
revision.status: Independent concept critique completed; generated-image review and 24-pixel visual proof remain with the parent study. Production identity is pending selection.

smallSizeRisks: A narrow or shallow central opening can close during rasterization, reducing the logo to a generic speech bubble. Keep the opening wide enough to remain visible at 24 pixels.
Domed shoulders and a sloping base can combine into a heart. The revised geometry depends on short level shoulders and a broad settled lower body.
An undersized or over-rounded tail may vanish at 24 pixels. The broad directional extension and its inner return must survive reduction.
Overemphasizing the M can turn the mark into a rounded letter badge. Recognition of speech should not depend on decoding the letter.
In the wordmark, an excessively narrow l may attach perceptually to M, while close u-v spacing can suggest w. Test the exact spelling independently of the symbol.
The upper aperture of a may close before the rest of the word fails; modest aperture enlargement should precede increasing the whole wordmark's weight.
opticalRules: Use a single connected filled logo path with one upper-edge negative incision and no enclosed counter.
Target body width to body height near 1.25:1, excluding the tail; tune optically after image generation.
Let the upper V reach roughly 45 percent of body height, leaving a broad lower bridge rather than a narrow connector.
Keep the tail near one eighth of the total height; at a 24-pixel mark it should remain a roughly 3-pixel directional feature.
No essential filled connection or meaningful negative opening should rely on a subpixel hairline at 24 pixels.
Round the notch vertex and tail tip just enough to avoid brittle points; preserve the shape's direction and the speech reading.
Correct horizontal centering for the left tail; judge perceived mass at 24 pixels as well as large scale.
Keep wordmark letterforms separated, preserve a distinct lowercase l, and space by optical gaps rather than monospaced cells.
Maintain exact Mluva case and spelling; retain JetBrains Mono provenance when producing eventual vector artwork.
Use opaque single-color ink or its light inverse; transparency belongs to the background, not the silhouette.
motionRelationship: The static shape carries the identity without animation. In a later film treatment, reveal the complete vessel with a calm opacity transition, followed by the wordmark as one stable line. A subtle expansion and return of the vessel's broad body may share the existing 3.4-second breathing cadence, with the tail and central notch remaining recognizable throughout. Keep the deformation very small; do not inflate the mark into a heart, mouth animation, liquid splash, or audio meter. The open notch may widen by a restrained amount during the breath while preserving its lower bridge. The opening and closing film appearances should settle on the exact same still silhouette. Reduced motion uses that steady mark. These are optional study directions and do not change the application's recorder-state meanings or promise any provider behavior.
